items.reason: "the more thankless you will go forever" keeps the old idiom 'go thankless' (= remain unthanked) in scrambled order; a first-time reader and a listener must reread it. Minimal fix keeps the sense.
items.new: So farewell, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am. You belong to that hopeless, sallow tribe that no wine in this world will ever warm, and for whom even Pale Sherry would be too rosy-strong; but with whom one sometimes loves to sit, and feel poor-devilish too, and grow convivial over tears, and say to them bluntly, with full eyes and empty glasses, and in a sadness not altogether unpleasant — Give it up, Sub-Subs! For the more pains you take to please the world, the more you will forever go unthanked! I wish I could clear out Hampton Court and the Tuileries for you! But gulp down your tears and hurry aloft to the royal-mast with your hearts; for your friends who have gone before are clearing out the seven-storied heavens, and making refugees of long-pampered Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael, in readiness for your coming. Here you strike only splintered hearts together — there, you shall strike unsplinterable glasses!

items.reason: "horse-whales" stops a modern reader and nothing nearby says what they are; Ohthere's horse-whales are walruses (hence the valuable teeth). Brief accurate gloss, once.
items.new: "He also visited this country with a view to catching horse-whales (walruses), which had bones of very great value for their teeth, some of which he brought to the king.... The best whales were caught in his own country, some of them forty-eight and some fifty yards long. He said that he was one of six who had killed sixty in two days." — Other or Octher's verbal narrative taken down from his mouth by King Alfred, A.D. 890.

items.reason: "Several whales have come in on this coast (Fife) in the year 1652": present perfect with a specific past date is not modern English grammar and trips the reader; simple past.
items.new: "Several whales came in on this coast (Fife) in the year 1652; one of the whalebone kind, eighty feet long, came in, which (as I was informed), besides a vast quantity of oil, yielded 500 weight of baleen. Its jaws stand as a gate in the garden of Pitferren." — Sibbald's Fife and Kinross.

items.new: "Once, when he was being pursued by a whale he had wounded, he fended off its attack for some time with a lance; but the furious monster finally rushed on the boat, and he and his comrades were saved only by leaping into the water when they saw the onset could not be avoided." — Missionary Journal of Tyerman and Bennett.
